question: Lanthanides are often called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**rare earth elements.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lanthanides** are a group of** metallic elements** that belong to the** f-block** of the periodic table.
 
• They are commonly known as rare earth elements because they are not found in large quantities in the Earth's crust and are difficult to extract.
 
• **Lanthanides have unique magnetic, optical, and catalytic properties that make them useful in various applications, such as electronics, magnets, and batteries.**
 
• Some of the lanthanides, such as **neodymium and dysprosium,** are critical materials for the production of high-tech products like smartphones, wind turbines, and electric vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkali metals are a group of elements that belong to the s-block of the periodic table and have one valence electron.**

 
 
• They are highly reactive and can explode when in contact with water or air.
 
 
 
• Inert gases, also known as noble gases, are a group of elements that belong to the p-block of the periodic table and have a full valence shell.
 
 
• **They are chemically inert and rarely react with other elements.**
 
 
 
• **D-block elements are a group of metallic elements that belong to the d-block of the periodic table.**
 
 
• They have variable oxidation states and are often used as catalysts or in the production of alloys.
